name: Shaphat (Elijah's father)
title: The prophet Elisha's father
summary: Shaphat was the father of the prophet Elisha and belonged to the tribe of Issachar. He was a wealthy farmer from Abel-meholah who owned land and had resources to keep twelve yoke of oxen for plowing. Through his son Elisha, his family became connected to one of the most significant prophetic ministries in Israel's history.

keyEvents.title: Elisha is called from the family field
keyEvents.description: The prophet Elijah found Elisha, Shaphat's son, plowing with twelve yoke of oxen on the family land. This shows that Shaphat was a wealthy landowner who could equip his son with substantial resources.

keyEvents.title: Elisha leaves home to follow Elijah
keyEvents.description: When Elisha was called, he slaughtered the oxen and cooked their meat using the plowing equipment as fuel, then took leave of his father Shaphat to follow the prophet Elijah.

keyEvents.title: Elisha's identity as Shaphat's son
keyEvents.description: Throughout his prophetic ministry, Elisha was identified as 'Elisha, son of Shaphat,' preserving his father's name in Israel's history.
